title.narrative: FCDO Supporting Adolescent Girls Education (SAGE) II Programme

description.narrative: Summary: Will support the access to non-formal education of 5,027 _x000d_ marginalised, out of school girls using evidence based and interventions that are proven in the SAGE to _x000d_ achieve results. These include ATL, vocational skills training, life skills support (CoGE) and safeguarding._x000d_ _x000d_ The SAGE component of TEACH project will support the access to non-formal education of 5,027 _x000d_ marginalised, out of school girls using evidence based and interventions that are proven in the SAGE to _x000d_ achieve results. These include ATL, vocational skills training, life skills support (CoGE) and safeguarding _x000d_ as follows: _x000d_ 1. Accelerated Teaching and Learning (ATL): the model delivers evidence based, innovative, gender_x000d_ transformative and inclusive community-based learning premised on qualified NFE community educators _x000d_ implementing accelerated teaching and learning (ATL) in community-learning hubs so that girls achieve _x000d_ Grade 5 competencies in literacy and numeracy. Using lessons obtained from the implementation of Covid_x000d_ 19 adaptations, the project will use different pathways so that girls access learning opportunities including _x000d_ face to face support pathways, telephone based and door to door pathways in the case of emergency _x000d_ situations such as cholera outbreaks, flooding and COVID 19. The project will also support the _x000d_ establishment of satellite hubs, linked to the main static hubs and nearby primary schools, to ensure that _x000d_ services are closer to girls’ place of residence. Continuous Professional Development (CPD) sessions will _x000d_ be provided for Community Educators (CEs) will be tailored to focus more on groups who have had the _x000d_ least access to education so far (GWDs and girls never been to school). The SAGE component of TEACH _x000d_ project will continue to support learners with transition to formal education and will prioritise girls who have _x000d_ never been to school as they are twice as likely to transition to education compared to other subgroups. _x000d_ The project will also continue to engage the Department of Social Development and MoPSE structures at _x000d_ community level to ensure that such learners are considered for the Basic Education Assistance Module (BEAM) which is a government led initiative that supports orphans and vulnerable children with school fees _x000d_ support. _x000d_ 2. Vocational Skills Training: The SAGE component of TEACH will support all eligible learners to access _x000d_ vocational training skills and will expand training opportunities to include enrolment in vocational training _x000d_ colleges. The project will also broaden the scope for ISOP skills training to include a theoretical component _x000d_ which covers business/enterprise skills development and financial literacy skills by working closely with _x000d_ relevant ministries such as Ministry of Women Affairs and Ministry of Youth. In addition to this, the project _x000d_ will also increase the amount of time that girls are supported on ISOP from the current 32 hours to 64 _x000d_ hours. To promote the uptake of non-female traditional vocational skills, the SAGE component of TEACH _x000d_ project will support the enrolment of at least 10% girls in vocational training colleges which are better _x000d_ equipped with resources for effective training delivery in areas traditionally considered to be non-female _x000d_ skills. _x000d_ 3. Champions of Girls education (CoGE): CoGE will be implemented to support agency, self-efficacy _x000d_ and empowerment using peer led approaches which will entail putting learners at the forefront of delivering _x000d_ sessions to their peers as opposed to having an adult facilitator. The project will also engage men and _x000d_ boys through CoGE through creating dialoguing platforms with men and boys around addressing negative _x000d_ gender norms which militate against girls’ ability to realize their full potential and to access education. _x000d_ _x000d_ The project will reach 5,027 marginalised and out of school girls in Mutasa, Mutoko, Chimanimani, Mutare Rural, _x000d_ Harare South, Reigate, Hatcliffe, Epworth, Imbizo, Khami and Bulilima.
